summary: Astro Scouts: A New Home is a web-based mission simulator that lets kids aged 7 to 12 train as junior astronauts. Players explore a lunar outpost in a top-down, Among Us–style view, move through the base, and complete hands-on missions such as repairing life-support systems, managing power and oxygen, and collecting samples. The game is level-based: players start on the Moon and then advance to Mars, where every level brings new challenges and real space facts. We built it because space careers feel distant to many children. Astro Scouts turns real NASA science into play, so kids learn how astronauts live, work, and solve problems as a team. The base map was designed using ideas and sketches from children themselves, so the game reflects what kids imagine a space home should look like. It runs in any browser, with no installation or sign-up needed.
details:
What it does and how it works. Astro Scouts is a browser game where each player becomes a junior astronaut living on a lunar outpost. Players walk around the base, interact with stations, and complete short missions that teach real concepts: low gravity, oxygen and power management, teamwork, and safety. Five playable characters (the “Astro Scouts”) make every player feel represented. After finishing the Moon missions, the crew moves to Mars, where new challenges appear in each level.

Benefits and impact. The game makes space science approachable and fun for children aged 7 to 12. It encourages curiosity, problem-solving, and STEM interest, and it is free, works on any device with a browser, and needs no installation. Our long-term goal is to use it in schools and at home.

Creativity. We involved children in the design. They sketched the base map, so the layout comes from their own ideas. The game combines a familiar, kid-friendly style (top-down exploration, pixel-art astronauts) with real NASA facts.

Tools and technologies. HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web game, using Phaser 3 and VS Code as the main development tools; pixel-art sprites for the playable character, the game map and interactive objects were made using libresprite and Tiled; AI-assisted tools for code and visuals (see below).

What we considered. Age-appropriate difficulty, clear and simple language, scientific accuracy, accessibility, and fun. We also thought ahead: our next steps are a full Mars mode, touch controls and sound, a probe mission with airlock exits to collect samples, and more NASA data.
